With every inline shellcheck directive stripped, only www-setup/src/install.sh remains (19x SC3043, local, runtime-probed by has_local at :39). Mirror template: 745 workflows, 740 distinct, 770 pipelines without pipefail.

Taskfiles: 99 files, 751 tasks, 954 cmds (116 multi-line). Real bash-only constructs: 4 in 2 files (ocx-mirror release.taskfile.yml:55,119,121; ocx satellite.taskfile.yml:183). task 3.53.1 mvdan/sh runs arrays, [[, declare -A, mapfile, local; errexit on and pipefail off by default; panics on associative keys containing '-'.

PowerShell: 26 files (13 authored), 0 BOM, 0 CRLF in authored; 25/26 parse clean on Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100, pwsh 7.4.7 and 7.6.6 (the failure is virtualenv's un-rendered template); 0 PS7-only syntax; #Requires -Version 5.1 in 2; Set-StrictMode in 2.
fish/nu/elvish: 10 files, only 3 authored (www-setup/src/install.{fish,nu,elv}, 650/547/566 LOC), all parse on fish 3.6.0, nu 0.105.1, elvish 0.21.0.
top_smells: Agent-written research scratch has no gate: 129 files at 79.2 findings/KLOC vs 4.9 for gated authored code (16x), 55% with no set flags, 2-space style outside the fleet's -i 4 -ci. The gap is the gate, not the model (ocx agents land at 1.4/KLOC under shell:verify).
Default-shell run: blocks hide semantics: 82% of fleet blocks and 96% of the mirror template run 'bash -e {0}' with no pipefail; only 4 jobs set defaults.run.shell.
${{ inputs.release_tag }} interpolated inside single quotes in run: (www-setup test-installers.yml:206-207) is the only real injection shape; fix is env: indirection.

bash-4 features and set -u + empty-array expansion behind #!/usr/bin/env bash with no BASH_VERSION guard (5 files, 6 files / 7 arrays); silently wrong on macOS bash 3.2 (local -A continues with an indexed array).
Gate scope gaps: git ls-files '*.sh' skips *.bash (4 bats helpers), 10 *.bats files (1997 lines) and extensionless hooks; 7 authored-shell repos have 0 files clean under -i 4 -ci.
set -e suppression inside functions called from conditions (SC2310 x69 in 9 files, SC2312 x150 in 41 files) is invisible without shellcheck -o check-set-e-suppressed, which no repo enables.
93 of 186 shebang scripts are committed mode 100644 (62 are ocx doc snippets), including grimoire/docs/public/install.sh.
oras-www/tools/*.sh: 47 findings in 406 LOC, cat | while read, unquoted vars, no set: the worst authored code.
patterns_worth_encoding: Dialect by shebang, honestly: 31 #!/bin/sh scripts with 0 bashisms; bash scripts say bash. Never put 'set -o pipefail' in #!/bin/sh (dash 0.5.12 exits 2, posh exits 1; measured).

The rustup local idiom with a scoped, reasoned shellcheck disable (www-setup/src/install.sh:5,39-40): has_local() { local _ 2>/dev/null; } / has_local || alias local=typeset. local works on all 11 POSIX shells measured; ksh93u+m leaves the variable unset.

Fleet gate recipe: 'shellcheck -S warning' plus 'shfmt -d -i 4 -ci' over git ls-files '*.sh' with fixtures excluded by pathspec (ocx/taskfiles/shell.taskfile.yml:38,48); extend the file list to *.bash and extensionless shebang files.
Strict header plus cleanup: set -euo pipefail for bash, set -eu for sh, trap cleanup EXIT next to mktemp -d (32 of 35 files), installers use 'trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM HUP'; no ERR traps.

Installer set: one directory, five dialects (sh/ps1/fish/nu/elv) sharing sed-able <TOKEN> placeholders; PowerShell side uses #Requires -Version 5.1, Set-StrictMode Latest, ErrorActionPreference Stop, -UseBasicParsing, TLS1.2 and a PSEdition check instead of $IsWindows (undefined on 5.1).
Checksum tool detection (command -v sha256sum else shasum -a 256) and no GNU-only flags in installers (0 date -d, grep -P, stat -c, find -printf, sort -V).

CI: defaults.run.shell: bash per job, explicit shell: pwsh on Windows, env: instead of ${{ }} for inputs; remember pwsh steps do not fail on mid-script native exit codes on 5.1/7.4/7.6 unless $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference is set (7.4+).
Taskfile cmds: errexit on, pipefail off by default; avoid printf -v, PIPESTATUS, read -p, BASH_VERSION and associative keys containing '-' (panics in task 3.53.1).
Small probe fixtures (b4.sh, emptyarr.sh, h2c.sh, pf.sh, gh_bash.sh, gh_pwsh.ps1, enc_nobom.ps1, tf/Taskfile.yml) are reusable as verification fixtures for rule depth files.
contradictions_of_frame: Fleet size: frame's ~1450 *.sh is the count before the sibling-clone exclusion (ablation stage 3 = 1433); real is 633 raw and 187 authored. Frame's 132 *.bash is 5 (4 authored bats helpers); 49 ps1 is 23; 22 fish / 21 nu is 6 / 3.
The ~1100 extensionless #!/bin/sh files are 389, of which 313 are ocx-generated gitignored trampolines; only 6 are authored (5 bd-managed hooks).

H1 is refuted: 0 of 190 sh-shebang scripts have SC3xxx (31 authored); the only local use is one deliberate, runtime-probed file. The real dialect risk is bash version (3.2) in bash-shebang scripts, not bash-in-sh.

H2 is only partly right: strict mode is common (77% of non-snippet bash) but is not cargo-culted into sh scripts and the named 'local x=$(cmd)' pattern is absent (0); the actual hazard is set -e suppression (SC2310/SC2312) and the bash 3.2 differences.
H4 does not hold for installers: they are POSIX and probe checksum tools; GNU-isms (sed -i x2, readlink -f x1, xargs -r x4) sit in test/manual scripts and the Swift check scripts.
H5 holds and is measured: 516 of 628 blocks use the default shell; pipelines run without pipefail; native non-zero exits do not fail pwsh steps on 5.1, 7.4.7, 7.6.6.

H6's 'agents fail most on bashisms under #!/bin/sh' is not what the fleet shows: agent sh scripts have 0 SC3xxx; their failures are unquoted expansions (SC2086), unguarded cd (SC2164) and absent strict mode.
Taskfile cmds are not limited to POSIX: task 3.53.1's mvdan/sh runs arrays, [[, declare -A, mapfile, local; only printf -v, PIPESTATUS, read -p, BASH_* vars and dashed associative keys fail.

headline_numbers: 24,527 shell-emission source lines across shell.rs+hook.rs+escape.rs+reconcile.rs+coexistence.rs, ocx_setup rc_block/profiles/shims/lib, ocx_cli activate/conventions/shell_state
363/363 unit tests pass for ocx_shell+ocx_setup at HEAD (5de9d777eb7d)
Hostile-value round-trip corpus 1: 982/989 ok (99.3%) across 10 shell targets x 43 values, via the real built ocx binary run through real interpreters
PATH-kind corpus: 642/667 ok; LIST-kind corpus: 636/667 ok with all 29 failures concentrated on posh (a POSIX quoted-glob portability bug)
0 version-floor failures across bash 3.2-5.3, zsh 5.0.8-5.9, 11 posix-family shells, fish 3.6.0-4.9.3, nu 0.105.1/0.116.0, elvish 0.21.0, pwsh 7.4/7.6.6, and real Windows PowerShell 5.1
rc-file idempotency: byte-identical tree after a second ocx self setup run
top_smells: PowerShell curly-quote injection: single_quoted_doubled (escape.rs:35) only doubles ASCII ', not PowerShell's Unicode quote-equivalence class (U+2018/2019/201A/201B); reproduced file-creation injection on pwsh 7.4, pwsh 7.6.6 and real Windows PowerShell 5.1 via the real emitted ocx output

Every ocx self setup rc-file write silently downgrades permissions to 0600, even starting from a plain 0644 .bashrc, with no documentation or opt-out (ocx_util::fs::write_bytes_atomic always builds its tempfile at 0o600)

A symlinked rc file (~/.zshrc -> dotfiles/zshrc) is replaced outright by a plain file on ocx self setup; the dotfiles-managed target is never written and the symlink is gone afterward - no symlink-aware code path exists anywhere in ocx_setup

posh (POSIX conformance-test shell) disagrees with every other measured POSIX implementation on export_list/remove_list_element's shared ${var%%"lit"*} construct, failing all 29/29 list-kind corpus values - low real-world severity since posh isn't a real distro /bin/sh, but a genuine portability counter-example

.bash_login-only login shells never get the ocx fence in the file bash actually reads at login (profiles.rs never targets or probes .bash_login), so activation silently fails to take effect for that login path
patterns_worth_encoding: Parity-test the emitted shell string against the equivalent in-process Rust computation (ocx's PARITY_ARMS + assert_every_present_interpreter_ran's three-way absent/broken/silent classification) - a strong, re-usable pattern for any multi-shell emitter, worth a shell-integration skill callout

Name escapers by quoting context, never by shell alone (fish_single_quoted vs fish_double_quoted), with a test pinned on the one byte that distinguishes them - ocx's own comment frames the risk precisely: "the wrong fish escaper is a shell injection"

Resolve PowerShell's $PROFILE via a live subprocess query rather than a hardcoded path table - the only correct strategy given OneDrive/GPO Documents redirection and the 5.1-vs-7 directory-name split (WindowsPowerShell vs PowerShell)

Any canonical 'hostile value corpus' this research program publishes should include the PowerShell curly-quote class (U+2018/2019/201A/201B, and presumably U+201C-201F for double-quoted) - four independently measured tools (ocx, direnv, starship, mise) all missed it, suggesting it's an ecosystem-wide blind spot worth naming explicitly rather than assuming ASCII-only hostile corpora are sufficient
contradictions_of_frame: H3 (ocx's escaping has edge cases in at least one of fish/nu/elvish/pwsh) is confirmed but sharper than hypothesized: not a conventional unescaped-metacharacter bug - every ASCII metacharacter is handled correctly in every shell - but a Unicode tokenizer-equivalence class specific to PowerShell that doubling the ASCII apostrophe cannot defend against, reproducing as real command execution on Windows PowerShell 5.1 itself, not just a pwsh 7.2+ convenience-feature quirk

H9 (nushell's version churn makes it the riskiest emitted-code target) is NOT supported by this surface: nu 0.105.1 and 0.116.0 produced byte-identical floor-test results for the full activation/hook/PATH stream, and the one plausible break point ($env.PATH's string-vs-list auto-conversion) is already guarded by a shared describe-check in both shims.rs and activate.rs. Zero nu-version-specific failures were found here - H9 may still hold for nu scripting idioms generally, but not for ocx's emitted integration code

The exemplar comparison contradicts an implicit assumption that mature prior art (direnv, starship, mise, zoxide) would be ahead of ocx on PowerShell escaping: all four use the identical doubling-only single-quote escaper and are equally vulnerable to the same curly-quote class - ocx is not behind the field here, the whole field has the same blind spot

Truncation guard 10/17; trap cleanup 8/17 (neither rustup nor cargo-dist traps); exit-code taxonomy 1/17 (www-setup); script-level rc editing 3/11 exemplars, 0/4 fleet; automated uninstall 3/17, 0/4 fleet.

Reproduced defects: BusyBox wget crash in www-setup on alpine:3.22 (rc=3), cargo-dist Rosetta precedence bug, k3s {1..3} loop runs once in 7/11 shells, docker --setup-repo swallows next flag in 11/11, posh rejects "$@" under set -u.
top_smells: Grimoire PowerShell front door (grimoire/docs/public/install.ps1:4-5) claims the cargo-dist installer verifies SHA-256, but the pinned cargo-dist 0.33.0 installer.ps1.j2 and its rendered output contain zero checksum/sha256/FileHash tokens. Template-level; generated release asset not fetched.

www-setup/src/install.sh (:352-354) and grimoire/docs/public/install.sh (:29) pass --secure-protocol/--https-only to wget unprobed. On stock alpine:3.22 (BusyBox 1.37, no curl) install.sh dies: `wget: unrecognized option`, 3 retries, rc=3, message blames the network. rustup guards with check_help_for.

www-setup/src/install.ps1:182 and :734 use `exit` while the documented usage is `irm | iex`; the host session dies on 3/3 engines (5.1, 7.4, 7.6). Scoop's Exit-Install (`$Global:LASTEXITCODE` + `break`) is the safe form.

Non-ASCII bytes (em dashes in runtime strings) in the curl-piped fleet sh installers: 114 bytes in www-setup/src/install.sh, 3 in the grimoire front door; yash in the C locale cannot read them. The ps1 is deliberately ASCII, the sh is not.

Fail-open integrity on the rolling path: www-setup warns and continues when no sha256 tool exists (install.sh:405) or the manifest row has no hash (:861); the pinned path is fail-closed. cargo-dist skips the same way (:354, :1773).

cargo-dist installer shipped to grim users: Rosetta check `sysctl .. 2>/dev/null || true | grep -q` has wrong precedence (template :1316): leaks sysctl stdout and picks arm64 when sysctl returns 0 for value 0; rustup has the correct form. It also downloads with plain `curl -sSfL`, no --proto or TLS floor.

Upstream defects in exemplars worth not copying: k3s `for i in {1..3}` under #!/bin/sh, docker-install `--setup-repo` double shift (dry-run becomes real), deno silent default to x86_64-linux-gnu (7/13 scenarios) and `curl -s` without -f, rustup/dotnet/nvm/brew with no download integrity.
patterns_worth_encoding: Truncation guard: body in main(), `main "$@"` as last line (or a { } block). 10/17 have it; deno and dotnet do not.

Declare one dialect, verify with the 11-shell `-n` set after proving each invocation on planted errors (55/55), polyfill `local` with has_local + alias typeset and a shellcheck disable comment; yash needs ASCII or a UTF-8 locale; nu-check needs an exit wrapper; use bash -n, not --posix, for bash files.
ASCII-only installer payloads: 11/11 exemplar sh and 5/5 exemplar ps1 are ASCII; non-ASCII breaks yash (C locale) and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (em dash decodes as 226,8364,8221).
Integrity with a root of trust other than the asset origin, a fail-closed `required` mode (www-setup verify_checksum), or a pinned hash (mold, vcpkg). Never print 'verified' on a path that can skip.

wget --https-only/--secure-protocol only after a --help capability probe (rustup check_help_for); BusyBox wget rejects both. curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused, never --retry-all-errors where a 404 fallback follows.
mktemp + trap on EXIT INT TERM HUP, expanded at definition when the variable is local (setup-grimoire, front door). Flagships rustup and cargo-dist have no trap.

Platform detection that fails loudly: explicit support matrix with exit 7, musl via ldd then /lib/ld-musl-* then /etc/alpine-release, Rosetta via (sysctl ... || true) | grep. Test with uname/ldd/sysctl stubs across ash, dash and bash 3.2 (13-scenario harness found 12 silent-wrong cells in 2 installers).
Documented exit-code taxonomy (0-7) and an offline test hatch (__OCX_TESTING_INSTALL_BINARY) so the real script runs end to end under every shell; 10 of 12 shell rows passed.

PowerShell installers: #Requires -Version 5.1, explicit Tls12, custom retry instead of 7-only -MaximumRetryCount, .NET ZipFile with zip-slip check, Get-FileHash, ASCII source, and never `exit` under irm | iex (use $Global:LASTEXITCODE + break).

Bash 3.2 floor patterns when macOS is a target: no empty arrays under set -u, awk tolower instead of ${x,,}, find -print -quit instead of | head -1 under pipefail; e2e passed on bash 3.2/4.0/4.4/5.3. A bash installer that may be piped to sh should guard on BASH_VERSION before the first bashism (Homebrew).
contradictions_of_frame: H1 contradicted for installers: 0 of 2 fleet #!/bin/sh installers have any shellcheck -s sh finding; 178 of 181 SC3xxx hits in the corpus are the deliberately polyfilled `local`. Real bashisms live upstream (k3s brace expansion, acme read -p and $'..').

H2 contradicted for the fleet: 0 masking `local x=$(cmd)` in the 4 fleet sh files (all 5 hits are dotnet-install); pipefail appears in 3/17, all bash; the two flagship POSIX installers use `set -u` only and handle errors by hand.

H4 largely contradicted: 0 GNU-userland true positives in fleet installers (regex false-positive rates 67-100%); exemplar hits are feature-detected (acme sed -i). Upstream is not strictly POSIX either: 3/11 exemplar sh files are bash by declaration.
H8 partly confirmed: only 1 of 3 fleet ps1 files targets 5.1 (www-setup, #Requires 5.1); setup-grimoire is pwsh-only by design; all 8 parse on 5.1, 7.4 and 7.6.

Frame item 3 is wrong for ocx: no ocx script installer exists (ocx/dist-workspace.toml:11 installers = []); the five dialect installers are in www-setup/src. setup-ocx is TypeScript (no shell to audit); grimoire-duo is a second checkout of the grimoire remote (8 byte-identical installer copies, deduped).

patterns_worth_encoding: Write one quoter per target shell from that shell's grammar. Never reuse `'\''` for fish (backslash is special in single quotes) or for nu and elvish (no `'` inside single quotes).
Use a data channel (JSON or CSV) where the shell can parse one, as direnv does for elvish, murex and json and mise does for nu env. Then nothing needs escaping.
Test every quoter against a 20-case hostile corpus through the real interpreter, byte-compared. Every defect found in this audit falls on that list.
Install bash hooks with a PROMPT_COMMAND that is string-or-array aware. Preserve the previous value and never assign a bare array when bash may be older than 5.1.
Give every hook a per-shell re-source guard: bash pattern check, zsh add-zsh-hook, fish function redefinition, pwsh `$global:` flag, atuin-style include guard. Elvish needs one too.
Use starship's two-phase init (stub plus `--print-full-init`) so bash 3.2 and POSIX-mode bash do not depend on `source <(...)`.
Emit ASCII-only expressions on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`[char]0xE9`), as oh-my-posh does.
Install nu support through the autoload dir, gate on `(version).minor` in the script, and pin the nu version in CI.
Cache init output on disk keyed by ConfigHash plus build version, written atomically (oh-my-posh), when generation is expensive.
Run per-shell tests with real interpreters in CI (direnv test/direnv-test.*, fzf tmux tests, omp e2e).
contradictions_of_frame: H3 confirmed in a narrower form. Escape bugs are not everywhere: 0 hand-written per-shell quoters failed where their syntax is supported, and all measured failures come from a shared POSIX quoter applied to fish, nu or elvish.

H9 only partly holds. nu has the highest flagged share among large-n shells (21%) and the most version pins (zoxide 11), but it has fewer total entries than bash and fish, and elvish is flagged higher (24%, n=21). Default emitted nu code from zoxide, mise and starship parsed on both nu 0.105.1 and 0.116.0 with 0 failures. The live nu failure was escaping, not version churn.

Bash pitfalls are narrow. The four non-omp emitters coexist on every bash version from 3.2 to 5.3, and escaping is not the bash risk. The real pitfalls are PROMPT_COMMAND array semantics before 5.1, `source <(...)` on bash 3.2/4.0/POSIX mode, and `$'..'` being unsupported on dash, yash and posh.

Version drift did not break default emitted code across 8 bash, 4 zsh, 4 fish, 2 nu and 2 pwsh versions. The version-dependent behaviours found were the pwsh empty-env semantics and the nu `run` keyword.
Test volume does not predict defects. mise has the most tests and the most measured defects, and direnv has fewer tests and none.
Startup cost does not track shell portability. It comes from mise's per-prompt hook-env, whatever the target shell.
